item.title: Grounded Together: Building Resilience, Connection, and Community — Wed Sep 16, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community ***P.S. this is part of a 5 week series, though not required, you are highly encouraged to attend all - No meeting on Oct 7***
Join **Rev. Rola Al-Ashkar** for a five-week journey exploring how our life experiences shape the way we respond to stress, conflict, belonging, and relationships. Through storytelling, guided reflection, and gentle body-centered (somatic) practices, participants will develop tools for greater self-awareness, emotional resilience, and compassionate listening. Whether you're seeking personal growth, healthier relationships, or a deeper sense of connection within our community, this series offers a welcoming and supportive space. No prior experience is necessary. Please register using the following link: [[LINK](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdxWVImvnFcRLw5on8gH2WFGQfoMnVmNowpxZd9FHajblr2Iw/viewform?usp=send_form)]. **Wednesdays:** Sept. 16, 23, 30; Oct. 14 & 21 6:00 – 8:00 pm
Source: Meetup: Mindful Embodied Spirituality

item.title: Photography Club of Davis — Wed Sep 16, 7:10 PM — Mary L. Stephens Davis Branch Library Blanchard Room
item.description:
The meeting will feature a photo critique of member-submitted images. Critiques tend to be positive learning experiences for both submitters and the general audience. Participants discuss “why does this image work” as well as “why does this image not work” and how the image may be improved. Attendees also learn about the techniques involved. The Photography Club of Davis meets every month on the third Wednesday of the month (except July and August) and welcomes members of the public to attend.
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

item.title: UN "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon — Fri Oct 23 — Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis
item.description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO) and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions.
Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.
Who:
The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.
Why:
Contribute to solving a problem in your community
Get experience working on a cross-f

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Wed Sep 16, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: NAMI Yolo County Presents Mental Health in Yolo County Jails Panel — Wed Sep 16, 6:00 PM — Episcopal Church of St. Martin
item.description:
A panel on mental health in Yolo County Jails. Join us for an important community conversation about mental health in Yolo County jails. Designed especially for family members and loved ones, the panel will bring together perspectives from the Yolo County Public Defender’s Office, and the Yolo County Department of Health and Human Services. Panelists will discuss the challenges people with mental health needs may encounter in the jail system, the services and resources available, and how families can better understand and navigate these systems when supporting a loved one. item.title: Author Event: Jason Dove Mark — Wed Sep 16, 6:30 PM — The Avid Reader
item.description: Jason Dove Mark @ The Avid Reader Wednesday Sep 16th, 2026 | 6:30 PM – 7:30 PM About the Book – The Earth Said Remember Me As the climate emergency worsens and biodiversity shrinks, we somehow get used to it. We struggle to remember what summers were like before the unrelenting heat, in those years before wildfires became an annual routine. We adapt, we normalize. Scientists call this “shifting baseline syndrome,” and they warn that it’s why we are increasingly sleepwalking toward disaster. In this inspiring manifesto, environmental advocate and longtime editor-in-chief of Sierra magazine Jason Dove Mark offers antidotes that everyone can use to resist ecological amnesia and make lasting progress to repair and revive a livable planet. The public is invited to this free virtual program designed for curious researchers at all levels and shown on the big screen. Does Google “know” anything about genealogy?
